issue: Brake-relevant wheel-speed signal accepted from CAN with no E2E protection (no CRC, no alive/rolling counter) and no SecOC/MAC; a spoofed or stale frame is trusted
Brake pedal request accepted from CAN with no authentication or freshness value
Vehicle-state / speed signal accepted with no E2E CRC or counter; used directly in slip control
Missing range / plausibility check on the wheel-speed sensor value: raw 16-bit value used directly, never checked against WHEEL_SPEED_MAX_RAW or against vehicle speed for plausibility
wheel_valid is set to 1 unconditionally on receipt; the RX_TIMEOUT_MS staleness logic and last_rx_ms are never used to invalidate inputs (no input-timeout monitoring)
UDS SecurityAccess uses a static constant seed (SECURITY_SEED) returned to every requester
Security key derived from seed by XOR with a constant (seed ^ SECURITY_KEY_CONST); trivially reversible
0x34/0x36 download path writes transferred blocks straight to application flash with no signature or checksum verification of the image
Ignored return value of a critical function: plt_flash_erase() result is discarded, so a failed erase is not detected before flashing
Ignored return value of plt_can_send() for the UDS reply (critical function return discarded)
goto-based error handling in the CAN transmit path
malloc/free of the CAN frame inside the 5 ms cyclic control task; dynamic allocation in a safety-related task
Recursion: diag_block_sum() is recursive (reachable from the cyclic task via sched_calibration_sum), so worst-case stack usage is unbounded
Main loop has no watchdog service and no program-flow / logic monitoring (ISO 26262-5 Annex D)
No requirement-ID traceability in source: no safety requirement references anywhere in the application code
No MISRA C compliance / deviation record and no coding-standard configuration in the repository (ASIL B expects an enforced coding standard with documented deviations)
No static-analysis configuration (no tool config for MISRA / data-flow analysis) in the repository
No structural-coverage / coverage configuration (ASIL B requires statement and branch coverage measurement)
No TARA (threat analysis and risk assessment) document for cybersecurity, required under UNECE R155 / ISO 21434
No safety case / safety plan / work products (hazard analysis, safety requirements) for the ASIL B item
